subject: Neuroscience
textbook: Neuroscience: Exploring the Brain, 3e (Bear et al.)
title: Synaptic integration
prompt:
Create a 29-second silent English 1920×1080 educational animation about Synaptic integration for Introduction to Neuroscience.
Use Remotion 4.0.410, React 19 and the introduction-to-neuroscience course kit. Reproduce the actual video in assets/source-kits/introduction-to-neuroscience/src/videos/ns04-synaptic-integration.tsx; fps is 30.
Keep the same dark course palette and diagrams. Use the actual state transitions from the source, not a generic neural-network animation.

Scene plan:
1. 0–6s, single: Signal travels down one dendrite; voltage rises by 10 mV then decays without crossing threshold. Why: A single small EPSP is subthreshold. Visible result: No axonal spike is generated.
2. 6–14s, temporal: Second signal travels the same dendrite; its EPSP adds to the remaining first EPSP and crosses threshold; outgoing spike appears after crossing. Why: Temporal overlap preserves enough depolarization to add. Visible result: Closely timed inputs can trigger a spike.
3. 14–21s, spatial: Signals converge from separate branches; sum trace rises by 18 mV and axonal spike follows crossing. Why: Inputs from different sites contribute to the same initial-segment voltage. Visible result: Spatial summation also reaches threshold.
4. 21–29s, inhibition: Third branch signal contributes downward voltage; visible EPSP components remain but combined trace drops below threshold and no outgoing spike occurs. Why: Inhibitory influence opposes depolarization in this simplified model. Visible result: Total voltage, not input count, controls firing.

All on-screen labels and narration-equivalent captions are concise English. Use no spoken audio or music. Preserve the specific objects, state bindings and timing above. Render the registered composition for this slug and inspect the final MP4 at the stored risk moments.
Reproduction requires the packaged TSX source, the course kit, Remotion/React dependencies, Chromium and ffmpeg. This prompt describes the reviewed artifact; it is not a self-contained promise of pixel-identical reproduction without those files.
final_title: Synaptic Integration: How Inputs Reach Threshold
learning_objective: Show that timed excitatory and inhibitory inputs combine at the axon initial segment and determine whether threshold is crossed.
core_conclusion: A neuron integrates inputs across space and time; a spike occurs only when the combined voltage reaches threshold.

requirement_prompt:
Create a 15-second silent educational animation in Manim Community Edition.

Explain “Synaptic integration” using this visual metaphor: “a glowing neural circuit carrying one signal for Synaptic integration”. Dynamically demonstrate the core formula or conclusion: Synaptic integration sums incoming potentials at one neuron..

Use one continuous scene and one clear narrative line. Explain only this concept; do not add comparisons, extensions, or side cases. Structure the motion in three connected beats:
1. 0–3 seconds: establish the objects, input, or initial state.
2. 3–10.95 seconds: show at least two causally connected state changes that reveal the mechanism and progressively connect key variables or conclusions to the visual.
3. 10.95–12.45 seconds: resolve the result, invariant, or central insight.

Keep introducing meaningful animation information until 12.45 seconds. Hold the final still frame for no more than 2.55 seconds.

All on-screen titles, labels, and supporting annotations must be short English phrases in Arial. Use a bright, non-black background (#F9F1F5); main visual (#15516C); secondary visual (#8F253B); highlight (#6E5300); and text (#172033). Maintain strong contrast and legibility.

Strict typography requirements:
- Render every complete title, label, phrase, or sentence as one native Text(...) object so every character shares one baseline.
- Never rebuild a line from separately positioned word or letter objects, and never align words by their individual bounding boxes.
- Create Arial text at a base font_size of 64, then uniformly scale the complete Text object to its final visual size; do not render explanatory text directly at a tiny font size.
- Preserve ordinary spaces inside the same Text object, set disable_ligatures=True, and do not add manual tracking, special-width spaces, or per-character offsets.

Use ThreeDScene for a genuinely spatial main visual: at least one core object must show volume, depth, or occlusion, and include one smooth camera move that reveals spatial structure. The 3D motion must clarify the concept rather than merely tilt a flat diagram. Render in 16:9.

Global rendering requirements:
- Never place plain English words, sentences, titles, or explanatory prose in MathTex, Tex, or inline LaTeX math mode. Use the native Text(...) component for all explanatory text and titles.
- If an English word is unavoidable inside a mathematical expression, explicitly wrap every word with \text{...}; never leave a word bare in algebra mode.
- Animate text at whole-word or whole-line granularity. Never split text into individually spaced letters or animate isolated letter spans.
- Do not use text-align: justify or the SVG textLength or lengthAdjust attributes.
- Use the final conclusion display as the video's opening poster frame; do not begin on an empty background.

production.scene_rationale: Four examples distinguish one decaying input, closely timed inputs, multiple synapses and an inhibitory subtraction. Each modifies real summation data and spike output, so it is not four captions on one unchanged trace. Scope uses a clearly labeled simplified linear model, not a claim that biological dendrites are always linear.
